targeted: Ordering decision before coding: F-MD-B18-A002-021's two remaining items (eligibility version, requiring a new ProducerRegistrySnapshot capture field; and read_model_version/serialization_version/executable_build_identity, described as needing a 'raw-capture decode capability') were reviewed against existing authority to determine which comes first. Re-reading ProducerRegistrySnapshot::capture() line by line while designing this work found that item 5, as previously scoped by F-021/E-046, was itself imprecise: only serialization_version and executable_build.build_id are real, already-captured fields (a decode-only gap); read_model_version does not exist anywhere in that capture at all (confirmed by grep) -- it is a missing-capture-field gap, the same category as eligibility_version, not a decode gap. This correction is recorded here rather than silently absorbed. The ordering itself is IMPLEMENTATION_DERIVABLE (infrastructure-before-consumer): building the general registry-content-decode capability in Reader is lower-risk (stays entirely within Reader/Admission, the layer already under active work this whole multi-turn arc) than reopening Capture, and the same decode capability would be needed regardless of when the new eligibility-version/read-model-version capture fields are added, so building it first is not an arbitrary choice -- it is the capability the Capture-reopening work would itself want to build on. This evidence implements only the decode-only portion of item 5 (serialization_version, executable_build_identity); read_model_version is explicitly reclassified alongside eligibility_version as 'requires a new Capture field', not touched here, and not silently folded into this fix.

probes.note: positive control: with a genuinely VERIFIED bound context whose registry_content carries real serialization_version/executable_build.build_id values, actualBoundInputContext() reports those exact values, not a live-config default

a VERIFIED bound context with no decoded registry_content at all reports empty string for both fields, proving the fix does not silently fall back to config('market_data.governance...') when the decode is unavailable -- the exact failure mode the original defect had

regression + strengthening control: B18ReplayComparisonExhaustivenessTest's mocks() stub extended with a real registry_content block; all eleven frozen-input perturbations, including serialization_version/executable_build_identity, still individually deny PASS when diverged, now against genuine decoded content

regression control: all pre-existing Seal tests (9) and Reader tests (4) re-run unmodified and green after adding the decode step to the shared verifyBoundContext() loop -- the new decode is additive (a new bundle key) and never changes any existing check's pass/fail outcome

root_cause_and_implementation: PublicationInputBindingService::verifyBoundContext() (shared by Seal and Reader) already fetches and hash-verifies every component's raw capture row (RunInputCaptureRepository::forRun()) inside its per-component loop, but only ever compared payload_hash -- it never decoded the row's semantic_payload_json. It now does so once, specifically and only for the registry_versions component (the one component whose precise sub-fields Admission needs), immediately after that component's existing payload_hash check passes: $decoded = $this->captures->verify($actualRow); $registryVersionsContent = $decoded['rows'][0] ?? []. This adds no new trust surface -- it reads only content whose integrity was already established by the unchanged check immediately above it, using RunInputCaptureRepository::verify(), the same decode method every other capture-completeness check in this codebase already uses. The decoded content is attached to the returned bundle ($bundle['_registry_versions_content']) and exposed through PublicationInputBindingService::readBoundContext()'s VERIFIED result as a new registry_content key -- additive, not replacing components/scope/component_manifest. ReplayVerificationService::actualBoundInputContext() now reads serialization_version from $boundContext['registry_content']['serialization_version'] and executable_build_identity from $boundContext['registry_content']['executable_build']['build_id'], each only when the bound context is VERIFIED and that specific decoded field is actually present (isset() checked precisely, not merely non-null) -- otherwise both report an honest empty string, never falling back to config('market_data.governance...') as before. read_model_version is unchanged, still reading live config: F-021's original framing grouped it with serialization_version/executable_build_identity as needing 'decode', but ProducerRegistrySnapshot::capture()'s payload has no read_model_version field at all (confirmed again by direct re-read of the file) -- decoding cannot produce a value that was never captured. This is recorded as a correction to F-021's own item 5 description, not silently absorbed into 'done'. Two targeted tests: test_serialization_version_and_executable_build_identity_come_from_decoded_registry_content_only_when_verified proves both the positive case (real decoded values reported exactly) and the fail-closed case (VERIFIED but no registry_content decoded -> empty, not config fallback). B18ReplayComparisonExhaustivenessTest's shared stub was extended with a real registry_content block so its existing eleven-field perturbation suite exercises genuine content for these two fields as well, not empty-string-versus-empty-string. No predicate was promoted: MD-S050-R0002/R0003's full eleven-field conjunction and MD-S050-R0014/R0071's registry-version bullet both still fail on read_model_version (unchanged, live config) and, for R0014 specifically, eligibility version (still uncaptured anywhere) -- both are still-open, still-deferred gaps, now precisely two items (not three), tracked in F-021.

scope_result.ordering_decision: IMPLEMENTATION_DERIVABLE: build the general Reader-side registry-content-decode capability before reopening Capture, since the Capture-reopening work (eligibility version, read_model_version) would itself want to expose its new fields through this same capability
